exposure: Daily vitamin D intake (400 IU/day vs. 800 IU/day)
outcome: Bone mineral apparent density (BMAD) at discharge
cohort: 215 very low birth weight (VLBW) preterm infants with birth weights under 1,500 g who were admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit.
finding: Daily supplementation of 800 IU of vitamin D was associated with improved bone mineralization (total body and femoral BMAD) at discharge in VLBW infants compared to 400 IU, even after adjusting for birth weight and duration of parenteral nutrition.
